Elevator pitch

Survey data is notoriously difficult to munge. Even when the data is recorded cleanly the options for ‘write in questions’, ‘choose from multiple answers’, ‘pick all that are right’, and ‘multiple choice questions’ makes storing the data in a tidy format difficult.

In 2014, FiveThirtyEight surveyed over 1000 people to write the article titled, America’s Favorite ‘Star Wars’ Movies (And Least Favorite Characters). They have provided the data on GitHub

Read and format project data 
# Include and execute your code here

# Path data
path = 'https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/raw/master/star-wars-survey/StarWars.csv'

# Loading in data
war = (pd.read_csv(path, encoding="latin1", nrows=1).melt())
war2 = pd.read_csv(path, encoding="latin1", skiprows=2, header=None)

Shorten the column names and clean them up for easier use with pandas. Provide a table or list that exemplifies how you fixed the names.

Shorten the column names and clean data 1 
# Include and execute your code here
war = (war
       .replace('Unnamed: \d{1,2}', np.nan, regex=True)
       .replace('Response', "")
       .assign(
               clean_variable=lambda x: x.variable.str.strip()
               .replace('Which of the following Star Wars films have you seen? Please select all that apply.', 'seen'),
           clean_data=lambda x: x.value.str.strip()
           )
           .fillna(method='ffill')
           .assign(
               column_df=lambda x: x.clean_variable.str.cat(
                   x.clean_data, sep="__")
           )
)

Shorten the column names and clean data 3 
# Include and execute your code here

replace_data = {
    'Response': '',
    'Star Wars: Episode ': '',
    ' ': '_'
}

war_use = (war
                .assign(
                    replace_dat=lambda x: x.value.str.strip().replace(replace_data, regex=True),
                    variable_replace=lambda x: x.variable.str.strip().replace(
                        replace_map, regex=True)
                )
                .fillna(method='ffill')
                .fillna(value = "")
           .assign(column_names=lambda x: x.variable_replace.str.cat(x.replace_dat, sep="__").str.strip('__').str.lower())
)

import pandas as pd
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import dataclasses as dat
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import tree
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn import metrics

# Path data
path = 'https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/raw/master/star-wars-survey/StarWars.csv'

# Loading in data
war = (pd.read_csv(path, encoding="latin1", nrows=1).melt())
war2 = pd.read_csv(path, encoding="latin1", skiprows=2, header=None)

####################
# GRAND QUESTION 1 #
####################

war = (war
       .replace('Unnamed: \d{1,2}', np.nan, regex=True)
       .replace('Response', "")
       .assign(
               clean_variable=lambda x: x.variable.str.strip()
               .replace('Which of the following Star Wars films have you seen? Please select all that apply.', 'seen'),
           clean_data=lambda x: x.value.str.strip()
           )
           .fillna(method='ffill')
           .assign(
               column_df=lambda x: x.clean_variable.str.cat(
                   x.clean_data, sep="__")
           )
)
war
war.column_df

# we want to use this with the .replace() command that accepts a dictionary.
replace_map = {'Which of the following Star Wars films have you seen\\? Please select all that apply\\.': 'seen',
                     'Please rank the Star Wars films in order of preference with 1 being your favorite film in the franchise and 6 being your least favorite film.': 'rank',
                     'Please state whether you view the following characters favorably unfavorably, or are unfamiliar with him/her.':'view', 
                     'Do you consider yourself to be a fan of the Star Trek franchise\\?': 'star_trek_fan',
                     'Do you consider yourself to be a fan of the Expanded Universe\\?\x8cæ': 'expanded_fan',
                     'Are you familiar with the Expanded Universe\\?': 'know_expanded',
                     'Have you seen any of the 6 films in the Star Wars franchise\\?': 'seen_any',
                     'Do you consider yourself to be a fan of the Star Wars film franchise\\?': 'star_wars_fans',
                     'Which character shot first\\?': 'shot_first',
                     'Unnamed: \d{1,2}': np.nan,
                     ' ': '_',
                     }
replace_map

replace_data = {
    'Response': '',
    'Star Wars: Episode ': '',
    ' ': '_'
}

war_use = (war
                .assign(
                    replace_dat=lambda x: x.value.str.strip().replace(replace_data, regex=True),
                    variable_replace=lambda x: x.variable.str.strip().replace(
                        replace_map, regex=True)
                )
                .fillna(method='ffill')
                .fillna(value = "")
           .assign(column_names=lambda x: x.variable_replace.str.cat(x.replace_dat, sep="__").str.strip('__').str.lower())
)

war_use
war2.columns = war_use.column_names.to_list()

####################
# GRAND QUESTION 2 #
####################

# Filter the dataset to respondents that have seen at least one film.

war_filtered = war2.query('seen_any == "Yes"')
Q1 = pd.get_dummies(war_filtered)

# Create a new column that converts the age ranges to a single number. 
# Drop the age range categorical column.
    
age = (war2.age
       .str.split('-', expand=True)
       .rename(columns={0: "min_age", 1: "max_age"})
       .min_age
       .str.replace("> ", "")
       .astype('float'))
age

# Create a new column that converts the education groupings to a single number. 
# Drop the school categorical column

education = (war2.education
             .str.split('-', expand=True)
             .rename(columns={0: "min_educ", 1: "max_educ"})
             .min_educ
             .str.replace("> ", ""))
education

# Create a new column that converts the income ranges to a single number. 
# Drop the income range categorical column. Create your target 
# (also known as “y” or “label”) column based on the new income range column

income = (war2.household_income
                .str.split(' - ', expand=True)
                .rename(columns={0: "min_income", 1: "max_income"})
                .min_income
                .str.replace("\$|,|\+", "", regex=True)
                .astype('float'))
income

war2.assign(min_income=income)
